segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״מִן הַכָּבוּשׁ״ — אֵין אָסוּר אֶלָּא מִן הַכָּבוּשׁ שֶׁל יָרָק. ״כָּבוּשׁ שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם״ — אָסוּר בְּכׇל הַכְּבוּשִׁים. ״מִן הַשָּׁלוּק״ — אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא מִן הַשָּׁלוּק שֶׁל בָּשָׂר. ״שָׁלוּק שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם״ — אָסוּר בְּכׇל הַשְּׁלוּקִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» One who vows that «pickled food» is forbidden «to» him is «prohibited from» eating «only pickled vegetables,» as that is what people usually mean when referring to pickled food. However, if he says: «Pickled food» is konam for me, and for «that» reason «I» will not «taste» it, «he is prohibited» from tasting «all pickled» foods. Similarly, one who vows that «boiled food» is forbidden «to» him «is prohibited from» eating «only boiled meat,» as that is the common meaning of the expression boiled food. On the other hand, if he says: «Boiled food» is konam for me, and for «that» reason «I» will not «taste» it, «he is prohibited from» eating «all boiled foods.»

positions.claim: 'pickled' means vegetables and 'boiled' means meat, unless phrased 'that I taste'
